Anatomy recognition · BR-013 / 014 / 015
CaseResultsTracesVerdict
Seven Sol trials · One Terra follow-up · 15 September 2026

How agents
recognize anatomy

Both models misnamed the same compact pancreas. Sol later recognized it with proposed names, an exact class inventory, or source CT. The follow-ups explain why a recorded miss can become a weaker task candidate.

One fresh attempt per condition. Existing segmentations supplied; whole-organ identities graded exactly.

01 / The original miss

One geometry.
Different identities.

Eleven objects are assigned from thirteen possible classes. Source spleen and gallbladder masks are empty; no cause or surgical history is asserted.

The compact purple object sits beside the larger orange loop. The original masks retain their source voxels and shared physical coordinates. The failed task supplies no CT and allows unused class names.

o197 · 43.4 mLPancreas
o277 · 63.5 mLDuodenum

Reference identities follow the source masks. Clinical cause and contour quality are outside the grade.

The conceptual crux

Recognize an atypical organ while deciding which classes are absent. A familiar silhouette can make the wrong inventory seem coherent.

02 / The follow-ups

The failure did not survive added context.

All three branches retain the central geometry. Each is a new task condition and fresh session, not a retry of A02.

BR-013 A02 / masks + broad vocabulary

Sol: 9/11
Terra: 10/11

Both call the compact pancreas “gallbladder.” Sol also calls the duodenum “pancreas.”

→ Proposed identities to auditA03 · Sol corrects both swapped names; no false repairs.
→ Exact 11 present class namesI01 · Sol recognizes every object: 11/11.
→ Original CT and prepared viewsC01 · Broad vocabulary restored; Sol recognizes 11/11.

These observations favor an inventory/evidence uncertainty hypothesis over a general inability to reason about anatomy. The contrasts do not isolate a causal mechanism from single attempts.

Fourteen matched oracle/no-op controls behaved as expected across seven task snapshots. All model sessions completed normally, with zero retries, a 1,800-second allowance and four CPUs/4 GiB RAM. Peak CPU/RAM use was not measured. Source lineage, exact answer replay, task hashes and runtime model/effort records are retained. This presentation verifies the frozen records without launching new trials.

04 / Trace analysis

What each agent actually did

Ordered actions, actual image payloads and public-message excerpts. Pseudocode summarizes the visible workflow; interpretations are marked separately.

1. Establish anchors

Read class names, positions, volumes and extents.

2. Isolate uncertainty

Render small groups and compare several views.

3. Test an interpretation

Use anatomy, spatial relationships and optional code-based probes.

4. Validate the artifact

Check ID coverage, allowed names and JSON structure.

No specialist medical inference model or new training was invoked in these traces. Supplied masks greatly reduce the problem: the agent recognizes and audits existing objects. A valid JSON file can still contain wrong anatomy.

Position narrows the search; local views finish the assignment

Pass

Recognize all 13 ordinary abdominal structures from existing masks and physical coordinates. The answer is one label per object; CT is unavailable.

73.4 s · 5 images · 3 commands · 2,035 output tokens · 13/13

    Read the vocabulary and helper-generated volumes, bounds and centroids; inspect the overview. The public assessment treats the large organs and long central vessels as well constrained.

    Write the 13 identities and check that every object appears once, each label is allowed and no label repeats. Independent grading confirms all 13 identities.

BR-013 · A02 / Sol/xhigh / 11 intact objects · 13 possible classes

Familiar silhouettes support a coherent but wrong assignment

Miss

The source scene has a compact 43.4 mL pancreas. Eleven objects must be assigned from 13 possible classes; unused classes are allowed. No mask voxels are altered and CT is unavailable.

157.6 s · 5 images · 7 commands · 5,015 output tokens · 9/11

  1. Concentrate on the central objects

    Read physical measurements and view the overview plus four focused renderings. The public assessment identifies the venous tree and interprets the broad transverse mask as pancreas. That mask is actually the source duodenum.

    Steps 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14

  2. Measure shape; leave the distance check unfinished

    Compute principal axes and extents. Attempt nearest-surface distances with SciPy, but the import fails and no replacement distance calculation follows. Instead, print three binary-mask maximum projections as ASCII shapes. These collapse depth; they are not individual CT slices.

    Steps 15, 16, 17

  3. Commit the wrong identity story

    Call the compact o197 object gallbladder and o277 pancreas, then infer that duodenum and spleen are absent. Validate the schema successfully. Grading finds two wrong identities: the intact pancreas and duodenum.

    Steps 18, 19, 20, 21
that mask is a single obliquely elongated sac, while the neighboring mask has the transverse head-to-tail geometry of pancreas.Public progress message · step 18

Interpretation

The public phrase “endpoint check” records an assessment, not a measured endpoint algorithm. This pass demonstrates effective use of prepared views and named categories. A helper example grouped a relevant vessel neighborhood, providing a focus hint even though it was not executed.

Primary lead / BR-017 M02

Partial absorption under broad audit

Best remaining failure-backed candidate in this anatomy series. Sol missed a 21.04 mL inclusion despite intact CT, all 13 labels, extensive views and normal completion.

  • Small exact deliverable: host, organ and one tolerant point.
  • Clean negative control and larger-inclusion positive control.
  • Observed cost: 404 s, 10,593 output tokens, about $1.011.

The focused two-mask version passed with identical data. Preserve the original broad scope when describing the failure. Repeatability and broad-scope robustness remain unmeasured.

Read the absorption experiment →
Secondary diagnostic / BR-013 A02

Atypical identity with uncertain class presence

A compact historical failure, with a weaker case for promotion. Sol and Terra both miss the intact pancreas. Sol takes 158 s and 5,015 output tokens, about $0.304.

  • No tiny mutation or exact boundary judgment.
  • Both models make the same pancreas/gallbladder error.
  • Sol passes with exact inventory, CT, or proposed names.

Keep it for studying open-inventory recognition. Mask-only identifiability remains unresolved; its difficulty may reflect missing evidence rather than a robust reasoning failure.

No robust, low-resource Sol-failure task is established yet. M02 is the strongest current lead; A02 is a useful secondary diagnostic. All passed conditions are retired as hard candidates.

Earlier micro-boundary DICOM misses remain historical evidence; their task-validity concerns were not resolved by this series. BR-010/011/012 were reassessment and curation, not additional model trials. The separate BR-016 aneurysm experiment has its own report and verdict.

Sources. TotalSegmentator source release for organ masks; ColonVessels and its data paper for the vessel case. Data and derived illustrations: CC BY 4.0. The experiment evaluates source-label identity, not a diagnosis, source-contour certification or clinical performance.
